items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Milton DeLugg; the name is only mentioned by the interviewer in the context of Tommy Newsom's employment.

ctx.x: Oh, he said he just got — Lionel Hampton said if you have any trouble with Benny, just get weirder than he is. And he did that, and I guess it worked for him at the time. Anyway, everybody’s got Benny stories. So you guys were kind of through the years have been alternating between big bands and combos and some studio work.

Yeah, I always play even, well Tommy was with the Tonight Show before I was. He was there with Skitch Henderson and Milton DeLugg. I started when Doc Severinsen started in 1967. But I always went right from there down and played someplace else. If it wasn’t the Half Note it was the Roosevelt Grill or something or the Plaza Nine. There was always some clubs.

Yeah, I asked Ross one day, you know because you spend your whole life working in gin mills and things, you know, low paying jobs, but the jazz scene is usually not high paying generally. And I asked him why he continued to work like down at the Half Note, down in the Village during the Tonight Show. Because you know you work all those years and you’ve got a nice paying job more or less, and he continued to work down there. And I think he explained it this way, he says, “I work at NBC to get cab fare to get down…
